_comment: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-06. There are no blocking content gaps.
This file used to claim '47 of 942 entries cannot ship' and that the cause was a SOURCE
limitation. Both claims were wrong. Thirteen of those entries DID carry a romanisation on
the page — the parser was welding the transliteration into the phrase field instead of
splitting the two — so they were a parser defect misdiagnosed as missing data, and the
count had drifted from reality for as long as it was hand-maintained.
pipeline/content/record-gaps.py now derives this file from the content linter's own output
and refuses to write when the lint is green, because 'there are no gaps' and 'the recorder
is broken' look identical from the outside and must not be collapsed into one another.
Current state: content lint PASS on 1045 records. The historical entries below are kept
because the diagnosis was wrong in an instructive way, not because the gaps are open.

resolved_2026_10_06.method: pipeline/harvest/reading.mjs replaced six rounds of character-class patching with structural reading of the page, verified against all 9,117 phrase rows on the twenty phrasebooks by pipeline/harvest/diff-parsers.mjs
resolved_2026_10_06.patched_by: pipeline/content/patch-blocked.py, which copies eleven readings verbatim from the harvest and re-parses every replacement before writing it
resolved_2026_10_06.fabricated_readings_discarded: 2918 rows across Latin-script languages, where the old parser filed part of the phrase or an English gloss into the pronunciation column

previous_claims_wrong_because: the thirteen were a parser defect, not missing data — the romanisation was on the page all along
the count was hand-maintained and had drifted; the linter is the only authority on it
